Issued at 138 PM CST Mon Nov 9 2026

Today - Tuesday: Dry and Warm

Benign weather expected the next day and a half as weak upper level 
ridging builds overhead. At the surface, a weak surface high 
will drift through the Northern Plains and Upper Midwest through
the day tomorrow, keeping conditions dry. Widespread warm air 
advection is taking place across the region with gusty 
southwesterly winds this afternoon behind a warm front. This has
allowed for temperatures along and south of the I-94 corridor 
to climb well above average into the low to mid 60s. A weak cold
front is not far behind, generally draped across the Twin 
Cities Metro area this afternoon and will continue to push east 
through the evening and overnight hours. While this will provide
a wind shift, there won't be an initial surge of cold air with 
this boundary. The cold air is lagging behind and will move in 
later this week (more on that later). As such, temperatures 
Tuesday won't take too much of a hit with most locations in the 
mid to upper 50s. NBM 09.13 probabilities for high temperatures 
at or above 60 degrees tomorrow are largely confined to 
Southwest Wisconsin and portions of West Central Wisconsin where
probabilities sit in the 50-75% range. An increase in cloud 
cover from the west will likely prevent areas west of the river 
from seeing highs above 60 tomorrow afternoon. 

Wednesday - Thursday: Light Rain Chances, Cool Down 

The pattern gets a little more active heading into midweek as an 
upper level trough drops out of the Pacific Northwest/Canada into 
the Upper Midwest/Great Lakes regions. With it, it will bring a 
modestly strong mid-level vort max and a surface low is expected to 
develop just south of our area across the Central Plains/Mid 
Mississippi Valley. With the surface low pressure center passing to 
our south across Iowa, precipitation is expected to develop on the 
north side of this low across portions of Minnesota and Wisconsin. 
While earlier forecast runs favored a more broad shield of low 
precipitation chances, recent NBM and LREF runs have favored a more 
banded scenario early on with a band of 850/700mb frontogenesis 
across Northern Wisconsin early Wednesday morning. From there, as 
the vort max starts to interact with increased mid level moisture 
across the area, scattered light showers may develop across the 
region. Better chances for rain continue to show up south and east 
of our area where lift and moisture are better co-located. QPF 
remains very light with NBM 09.13 probs for 0.10 inches at less
than 20 percent for most of the area (apart from Taylor County 
where frontogenesis showers could lead to increased totals - 
still low confidence 25-30 percent). Even NBM 90th percentile 
totals have come down from previous forecasts with 0.10-0.20 
inches the new high end range. Rain remains the favored 
precipitation type as the cold air intrusion looks to lag behind
the time that the precipitation is mostly likely to be falling 
during the day on Wednesday. If the cold air moves in faster or 
precipitation hangs on for longer into the evening/overnight 
hours, a few flakes could mix in (this is more probable up in 
North Central Wisconsin). If any snow does mix in, it is not
expected to accumulate. 

Temperature wise, the surge of cold air looks to come late Wednesday 
evening into the overnight hours. Lows Wednesday night could drop 
into the mid to upper 20s for West Central Wisconsin with low 30s 
elsewhere. High temperatures Thursday will be significantly cooler 
from the start of the week in the upper 30s to lower 40s. Would not 
be surprised if current forecast temperatures for late week are too 
high given that forecast 850mb temperatures will be in the -5 to -8 
deg C range. It's very possible that due to the recent string 
of warm weather that a warm bias is being added to these 
temperatures. Will stick with the blended solution for now but 
this will be something to monitor over the coming days. 

Next Weekend: High Pressure Sets In 

A Canadian high pressure is expected to sink south into the Upper 
Midwest by Friday, dominating much of the weather pattern across the 
Central CONUS by Saturday. This will keep conditions dry so apart 
from the light rain chances on Wednesday, a dry forecast is on tap 
for the area through at least early next week. Temperatures will be 
at their coolest Thursday into Friday with some recovery expected by 
Saturday into the upper 40s.
